newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM sells oil/gas business to Santos.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM sells oil/gas business to Santos.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Monday it has sold its oil and gas business to Santos Ltd for A$45.1 million.
The sale excludes MIM's south-west queensland oil and gas properties and MIM's equity in Western Australian exploration permit WA-235P, where the Marsi well is due to spud this week, MIM said.
MIM said its oil and gas business did not fit strategicaly with the company's focus on copper, gold, coal, lead, zinc and silver.
Proceeds from the sale would contribute to the development of MIM's new projects, the company said.
Santos would employ most of MIM's oil and gas workers, the company said.
Santos said on Friday it was interested in bidding for MIM's oil and gas interests and would consider a number of acquisition opportunities in the next year.
Santos said the acquisition provided a basis for the company to grow in Papua New Guinea and Indonesia.

The interests acquired by Santos include a 20 percent stake in PPL56, which takes in a 6.975 percent stake in the SE Gobe oil field and various exploration prospects in the Fold belt area in Papua New Guinea, Santos said.

The sale also gives Santos a 33.33 percent holding in the Bentu PSC gas development project in Indonesia, along with stakes in exploration projects in the Carnarvon Basin offshore of Western Australia.
MIM's estimate of the reserves in the portfolio is 16.8 million barrels of oil equivalent, including 5.8 million barrels of oil reserves, Santos said.
SE Gobe is part of the larger Gobe project, which involves development of both the Gobe Main and SE Gobe fields.
Oil production from SE Gobe is expected to start in the first half of 1998, with initial production put at about 25,000 barrels of oil a day, Santos said.
The Bentu project is located in central Sumatra, about 800 km northwest of Jakarta.
The block, in which Santos already holds a 27.78 percent interest, contains proven recoverable gas reserves and is expected to come on stream in around 2000, Santo said.
Santos said it would fund the acquisition from existing cash facilities. The bid also is subject to regulatory approvals and satisfaction of certain other conditions.
An MIM spokesman told Reuters MIM was considering the future of its Southwest Queensland gas well, which was excluded from the sale.
